title: Detection of OXA-48-like, KPC and NDM carbapenemases from blood cultures
author: Axel Hamprecht
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rtrd6m6

steps.title: Collect blood culture fluid
steps.instruction: Draw 1–3 ml of blood‑culture fluid from positively flagged bottles that show Gram‑negative bacilli on Gram‑stain and transfer 1 ml into a 1.5 ml reaction tube (e.g., Eppendorf).

steps.title: Lyse cells with SDS
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl of 10 % SDS to the tube, invert and vortex, then incubate 5 min at room temperature. Centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 g in a microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Wash pellet
steps.instruction: After centrifugation a white pellet should be visible; if it is smaller than shown, increase the starting volume. Gently remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, add 1 ml ddH₂O, vortex or resuspend with a pipette to obtain a homogeneous suspension, and centrifuge again 1 min at 13 000 RPM. Remove the supernatant. If the pellet is white/grey with few erythrocytes proceed; if still red, repeat the washing step with ddH₂O or PBS.

substeps.instruction: Check pellet size; increase blood‑culture volume if pellet is too small.
Assess pellet colour; repeat wash with ddH₂O or PBS if still red.

steps.title: Add LY‑A reagent
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant gently, snap the bottom of the tube with a finger and/or vortex to detach the pellet, add 10 drops of LY‑A solution (provided with RESIST‑3 O.K.N.) and vortex (or pipette up‑and‑down) until a homogeneous suspension is achieved.

steps.title: Apply sample to ICT cassette
steps.instruction: Pipette 90 µl of the suspension into the sample field of the ICT cassette and incubate up to 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Interpret ICT result
steps.instruction: The test is valid when a red control line appears at position ‘C’. Presence of a band at ‘O’ indicates OXA‑48‑like, at ‘K’ indicates KPC, and at ‘N’ indicates NDM. OXA‑48‑like and KPC bands appear within 30 s–2 min; NDM bands appear in 2–7 min (sometimes up to 15 min) and are usually fainter. Any band appearing within the 15‑min reading window is considered positive. If a K or O band appears early and you wish to exclude NDM, read the test again at 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Note timing of band appearance (30 s–2 min for OXA‑48/KPC; 2–7 min, up to 15 min for NDM).
If needed, re‑read at 15 min to detect late NDM bands.

steps.title: Optional ZnSO₄ enhancement
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl ZnSO₄ solution to the suspension and incubate in a heating block for 15 min at 37 °C while shaking at 300 rpm (room‑temperature incubation without shaking is possible but not extensively tested). This step improves detection of NDM‑producing isolates.

steps.title: Validate and troubleshoot
steps.instruction: Test the ICT with several previously characterized OXA‑48, KPC and NDM isolates to become familiar with the procedure. If the pellet (or most of it) is lost during washing/centrifugation or is initially too small, repeat steps 1–4 to obtain a sufficient pellet before proceeding. A small pellet can cause false‑negative results, especially for NDM. The short protocol (without the ZnSO₄ step) works well for OXA‑48 and KPC and most NDM isolates; faint NDM bands can be improved by the additional ZnSO₄ incubation (advanced protocol).

substeps.instruction: Run the assay on known OXA‑48, KPC, and NDM isolates.
If pellet loss or insufficient size occurs, repeat steps 1–4.
Use short protocol for routine OXA‑48/KPC and most NDM; add ZnSO₄ step for weak NDM signals.
